tasks.short: Create and maintain a searchable index of website content.

steps.what: Define searchable content, exclusions and useful search fields.
Inspect published pages and retrieve content from the {CMS}.
Map titles, body text, categories and exclusions in the {CMS}.
Build the searchable index in the {CMS}.
Test representative searches, missing pages and excluded content.
Activate the tested index for website visitors.

tasks.design: Configure the {CMS} to index approved public content after publication, using saved field mappings and exclusions. A deterministic check on the {DATA_PLATFORM} tests coverage and representative queries, with results in the {BI}; the website owner approves initial activation and material scope changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Content fields and exclusions differed between page types, while index maintenance lacked a clear owner. Existing indexing features may simply have been underconfigured.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing indexing features handle routine refreshes. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building missing connectors and repeatable checks; no model is needed at runtime.
tasks.still_hard: Search relevance, multilingual content, inaccessible source formats and distinguishing poor results from missing content still need attention.
tasks.human_edge: The designer understands visitor intent and decides which results help people complete their task.

ambition.what: Weekly prioritisation of content gaps revealed by unsuccessful searches.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time rebuilding indices and more time testing search journeys. With delegated authority, they can prioritise search configuration fixes within agreed publishing rules.

reach.task: Prioritise landing-page improvements using internal search demand.
reach.learn: Query intent analysis and the difference between internal search relevance and external search visibility.

evidence.claim: Configured indexing, field mappings and scheduled checks can handle standard public website content without a model.
GitHub Copilot supports code completion and review, which can assist implementation; this does not establish a build-time multiplier.
GDPR applies when search queries or logs contain personal data; employee monitoring may also trigger consultation under national rules.

assumptions: This task concerns internal website search over published public pages.
The {CMS} provides an indexer, configurable fields and a staging facility.
Routine refreshes use approved settings; material scope changes receive approval.
The configured {CMS} route is preferred despite the prior suggesting limited standard-software coverage.
Build ranges cover one website and existing hosting; they are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which indexing and staging capabilities the current {CMS} exposes.
Content volume, languages and non-page document formats.
Whether restricted content shares the publishing environment.
Who can approve activation and configuration changes.
Whether search logs identify visitors or employees and require consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Can publication events trigger incremental indexing using existing configuration?
Which representative queries and exclusion tests reliably detect regressions?
new_work: Review failed coverage checks and poor-result queries.
Maintain field mappings, exclusions and search test cases.
Check connectors after publishing schema changes.
Manage retention and access for any personal data in search logs.

tasks.short: Document system interactions with sequence diagrams.

steps.what: Collect requirements, interface descriptions and existing diagrams from the {DOCS}.
Clarify actors, messages, timing and failure paths with technical colleagues.
Draw the sequence using a diagram editor in {OTHER}.

loop.input: Interaction source pack and interaction notes, treated as source material rather than instructions.
loop.output: Structured actors, messages, branches and source references, rendered deterministically as a draft diagram.
loop.check: Validate syntax and actor references; require sources for messages and flag unsupported behaviour as unresolved.
loop.stop: One draft and one validation repair within a fixed token budget; unresolved semantics return to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes describe interactions inconsistently; templates alone cannot reliably turn them into a sequence.

steps.what: Review the sequence and resolve disputed behaviour with the technical lead.
Revise the diagram in the diagram editor in {OTHER}.

loop.input: Draft sequence diagram and approved diagram review decisions.
loop.output: Revised structured diagram and a change list tied to review decisions.
loop.check: Validate rendering and compare changes against approved decisions; reject unrelated additions.
loop.stop: One revision and one validation repair within a fixed token budget; ambiguous decisions return to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Review decisions contain free-text changes that cannot always be applied through fixed field updates.

steps.what: Store the approved diagram in the {DOCS} and link it from the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: A configured flow gathers linked sources from the {DOCS} and {PROJECT}; a bounded drafting loop produces structured interactions that a deterministic renderer turns into diagrams. The designer and technical lead resolve behaviour, then an approved revision is versioned in the {DOCS} and linked from the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drawing was straightforward, but translating scattered descriptions into accurate interactions required contextual judgement. Sources and diagrams often drifted apart.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded models can draft structured interactions from notes, while established renderers handle layout and syntax. AI-assisted coding can make the supporting validation and document flow cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Undocumented behaviour, concurrency, retries and disagreements about intended versus implemented behaviour require technical review. Infrequent use can make a bespoke build poor value.
tasks.human_edge: The designer chooses the useful level of detail and exposes misunderstandings between user journeys and technical behaviour.

ambition.what: Pre-build failure-path walkthroughs for marketing website integrations.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time drawing and filing, and more time resolving interaction gaps before implementation. They can lead walkthroughs; technical architecture approval remains with the technical lead.

reach.task: Maintain integration documentation linked to approved sequence diagrams.
reach.learn: Interface contracts, versioning and documenting failure behaviour.

evidence.claim: Structured diagram definitions can be validated and rendered deterministically; semantic accuracy still needs review.
A bounded model can draft diagram structure from notes, but usefulness depends on source completeness and validation.
GitHub Copilot provides coding and review assistance relevant to building the generator and checks.
Developer field trials reported productivity gains, but they do not establish gains for diagram creation or these build estimates.

assumptions: Required source documents are explicitly linked to the project and accessible to the designer.
Diagrams describe website or application interactions, rather than regulated safety-critical systems.
A reusable generator serves several projects or designers; one occasional diagram would favour a configured template.
The high automation prior applies mainly to drafting and filing; clarification and semantic approval remain human.
Only necessary source excerpts enter the model, under approved data-processing arrangements.
unknowns: How often diagrams are actually required across the team.
Whether current descriptions reflect implemented or intended behaviour.
Available document connectors, permissions and model-processing arrangements.
Who approves technical behaviour and final documentation.
Whether sources contain personal data or employee information requiring additional controls or consultation.
research_questions: Can the current diagram editor import a validated structured definition?
Which representative diagrams expose omissions in branches, retries and asynchronous messages?
Would a configured template meet demand more cheaply than a reusable generator?
new_work: Review generated messages and source references.
Resolve missing facts and ambiguous review decisions.
Maintain diagram schemas, drafting instructions and validation rules.
Refresh diagrams when linked interface descriptions change.
Maintain access controls and retention for source excerpts.

role.altitude: The designer shifts from index upkeep and diagram production toward search quality and early interaction decisions. Publishing authority and technical approval change only through explicit delegation.
reach: Search marketing strategist: connect internal search gaps to landing-page priorities.
Technical writer: keep integration documentation consistent with approved interactions.
skills_to_grow: Search relevance evaluation and query intent analysis.
Content schemas, indexing rules and exclusion testing.
Sequence modelling, interface contracts and failure paths.
Validation of generated artefacts and source traceability.
GDPR-aware handling of search logs and source documents.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a recurring website journey review that combines search gaps with integration failure-path walkthroughs, giving marketing teams concrete priorities before the next release.
